acv.quote: Two hundred and fifty K ACV.

data.reason: Halima, the COO, picked the rival because it brought named people and on-call cover for on-sales. Our support tiers sounded like 'a queue with a faster timer.' Jordan thought the load test had won it.

trigger.action: Lead with who answers when payments fail mid on-sale.
trigger.why: Payments failed four minutes into an arena on-sale, and the old provider replied only after it ended.
trigger.quote: They got a reply after the on-sale was over.

decider.action: Speak to the COO about a failed on-sale, not load tests.
decider.why: Halima decided alone in one meeting. Ben, the CTO, wanted us, and her only answer to his load test was 'good.'
decider.quote: it was Halima's call and she made it in one meeting.

competitor.action: Name the people and on-call cover behind big launch days.
competitor.why: Ben said the rival brought its real account team and promised on-call cover. Jordan's view that this over-promised is only his guess.
competitor.quote: someone on call for every major on-sale

message.action: Replace tiers and response times with the named person who answers.
message.why: When Halima asked who her person was, Jordan's walk through support tiers turned her against us.
message.quote: so it's a queue with a faster timer.

proof.action: Show on paper who watches and answers on on-sale morning.
proof.why: Halima asked for an on-sale plan, and we had none. Jordan also had no ticketing customer to vouch for us.
proof.quote: She wanted to see, on paper, what we do on an on-sale morning.

words.action: Say 'what happens when it's down,' not uptime history.
words.why: Halima and her team never said 'support.' They asked 'who,' and she rejected uptime as the reason to buy.
words.quote: I don't buy uptime, I buy what happens when it's down.
